newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 23.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- CABLE & WIRELESS IN BROAD TELECOMS MERGER

Competition in UK's telecoms market took a dramatic new turn on Tuesday with the announcement of a four-way merger involving Cable & Wireless's telecoms business Mercury and three cable groups - Bell Cablemedia, Nynex and Videotron. The new company, to be called Cable & Wireless Communications, will be the UK's biggest cable and communications group, with a potential value of 5bn stg. The move represents the strongest challenge yet to the dominance of British Telecom in the UK residential telephony market.
-- DENMARK BLOCKS EU RIPOSTE TO ANTI-CUBA LAW

Plans by the European Union to retaliate against US trade sanctions against foreign firms dealing with Cuba have suffered a setback after Denmark pledged to vote against the measures. Denmark said that the proposals, aimed at protecting EU companies from the US Helms-Burton Act, would compromise Danish sovereignty. However, EU officials have claimed that Denmark's opposition is based on a political rather than legal motivation.
-- "TICKETLESS" AIRLINE TRAVEL SET TO SPREAD

The International Air Transport Association will this week announce details of standards for electronic ticketing, due to come into force in June 1997. Under the new system, travellers use the credit card on which they purchased their flights as "tickets" when they get to the airport. In the future, new "smart-cards" may be used for both travel and immigration procedures. Computer giant IBM announced a deal Tuesday with Bermuda international airport to pioneer its "FastGate" immigration smart-card.
-- INDUSTRY UPTURN SET TO INCREASE, SAYS CBI

The latest industrial trends survey from the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) claims that the upturn in British manufacturing is set to accelerate in the coming months. The survey notes a marked improvement in manufacturers' optimism, and a strong upturn in new orders. Andrew Buxton, chairman of the CBI's economic affairs panel, also claimed there was little concern that the stronger pound is causing problems.
-- BRUSSELS PLAN ON MERGER ATTACKED

Britain's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) has joined with its German competition authority counterpart to criticise plans by the European Commission to increase the powers of Brussels to vet European mergers. John Bridgeman, director of the OFT, warned that the proposal would result in a "significant centralization of merger control" in the European Commission. The Commission is proposing lowering the turnover thresholds of companies covered by European merger regulation, a move which would roughly double the number of mergers vetted by Brussels.
-- LLOYDS OF LONDON BACKS CALIFORNIA QUAKE PLAN

Lloyds of London is to provide 200m stg of a total of 300m stg reinsurance cover to be provided by the London insurance market for a new body which protects homeowners in California against catastrophe. The new group, the California Earthquake Authority, is a state-sponsored body established to help solve California's homeowners' insurance crisis following the 1994 Los Angeles earthquake.
-- OFTEL BANS BT VENTURE WITH BSKYB

The UK's telecommunications industry regulator Oftel has banned a joint promotion between British Telecom and the satellite broadcaster BSkyB. Under the alliance, members of BT's Friends and Family discount scheme were offered a number of free calls if they were also subscribers to BSkyB satellite television. Oftel director-general Don Cruickshank said the promotion was in breach of BT's licence. BT has said it will comply with the order, but that they are baffled as to its basis and that a legal challenge has not been ruled out.
-- US COMPANY TO INVEST 45.7 M STERLING IN NORTHERN IRELAND

US electronics company AVX is to invest 45.7m stg upgrading its factory at Coleraine, Northern Ireland. The news will boost the foreign investment effort of the province, particularly after recent uncertainty over the prospects for peace. AVX manufactures ceramic capacitors for the consumer electronics, motor and telecommunications industries.
-- TELEKOM DEBTS "OFFER TAX EFFICIENCY'

Analysts at investment bank BZW have said that concerns over the high debt levels at Deutsche Telekom, the German telecommunications giant currently the subject of Europe's largest-ever initial public offering, may be misplace because the debt is surprisingly tax efficient. But the report from BZW, the investment banking arm of Barclays Bank, also warned that on key indicators such as dividend yeild Deutsche Telekom compares badly with rivals such as British Telecom and the Dutch group KPN.
--US GROWTH DRIVES SMITHKLINE RISE

Healthcare and pharmaceuticals group SmithKline Beecham has reported a 20 per cent in third-quarter pre-tax profits, to 374m stg. Sales rose 15 per cent, to 2bn stg, with particularly strong growth in the US where pharmaceutical sales rose 33 per cent. The figures, which were in line with analysts' expectations, also revealed a 25 per cent rise in spending during the quarter on research and development.
